metadata.description: Standards bypass configuration for this branch

bypass.reason: Pure utility — deep_merge and backup_json only. No operational side effects to log. Migrations archived.
Pure data registry — dict lookup only, no operations to log
Pure utility — branch name extraction and normalization, no side effects
Pure string transformation — placeholder replacement engine, no file I/O

Pure reader — parses the owner's .updateignore and answers is_ignored(). Performs no operation: it never writes, and spawn never creates or modifies the file. The operation it informs is the update itself, which update_ops logs at the site that performs it (log_operation('update_executed')).

Pure reader (DPLAN-0351) — returns the docs page skeleton text and writes nothing, so there is no operation here to log. The operation it serves is @seedgo's docs_page render, which seedgo performs and logs in its own process.

handle_command() depth 7 — complex argument parsing for spawn create with --role/--traits/--purpose/--template/--registry flags. Nested while loop through args array; extraction would obscure control flow.

update_branch() depth 4 — 10-step orchestration workflow (resolve, load registry, load meta, reconcile, detect changes, dry-run, execute changes, refresh meta, post-flight, return). Nesting serves workflow structure.
regenerate_template_registry() depth 5 — dual-pass tree scan (directories then files) to build registry with correct IDs. Nesting inherent to algorithm.

save_branch_meta() depth 5 — atomic file write with try-except-cleanup for temp file pattern. generate_branch_meta() depth 5 — triple-loop adoption path matching (path-first, then hash). Both justified.
sync_registry() depth 6 — iterates branches, checks passport, loads template registry, generates branch_meta. Nesting inherent to multi-step registry rebuild.
_print_branch_summary() depth 6 — nested formatting of reconciliation results with per-category output. Display logic requires nested iteration.
Pure registry generation — walks template, hashes files, builds registry. Uses meta_ops.compute_file_hash and json.dumps directly. Not an operational handler.
load_branch_meta() no longer called by P1 engine but has tests and may be reused by sync-registry or P2 shared library.
Local import of render_all_meta_tabs from memory.apps.handlers.tracking.tab_renderer — @memory has no module entry point for this API. Cross-branch contract per FPLAN-0286.

backfill_owner_and_registry_id() is a migration function for TDPLAN-0012 — called manually to backfill existing registries. is_owner() is part of the frozen interface contract (TDPLAN-0012) — consumed by @ai_mail and @devpulse via direct import.

Pure I/O primitive — stage/fsync/os.replace only, same species as json_ops.py above. Nothing to log: it is the write mechanism every other handler's log_operation call ultimately rides on, and logging each atomic write would emit an entry per passport/registry swap. Verified load-bearing in BOTH lanes 2026-08-16 (checklist [FAIL] json_structure; audit 97%/overall 99% with it lifted).

Pure read-only predicate — reads the template's manifest and walks its tree to return the list of files a mint failed to deliver. Same species as placeholders.py/class_registry.py above: no mutation, no operation of its own to log. The operational event IS logged, at the decision point where it belongs: core._spawn_agent emits json_handler.log_operation('mint_refused', ...) on the refusal, beside the existing 'branch_created' record. Verified load-bearing in BOTH lanes 2026-08-17 (checklist [FAIL] json_structure; audit Json_Structure 97% / overall 99% with it lifted).

Routing only since fleet green leg 9 (spawn's decision): the mint lane moved whole to handlers/mint_ops.py spawn_at, and its operations are logged there at the decision points (mint_refused for a retired or forbidden class, mint_refused for a missing file, branch_created). core now parses create's flags and hands in its meta-tab importer; it performs no operation of its own to log. File-wide because json_structure passes no line.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): cli_flags takes every file directly in apps/ as an entry point, and its own scope comment says apps/{name}.py. This file is the package marker, one line (from . import handlers), never run; the entry point is apps/spawn.py, which passes cli_flags. File-wide because cli_flags passes no line.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): tests/__init__.py is the package marker of the suite, not a test module. It carries the META header (item 5, cured in leg 8), but items 6 and 7 ask for the module it tests and a declared pass, and it tests nothing; the checker already judges conftest.py on item 5 only for the same reason (a conftest has no subject).

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): '' is never an answer here. The success path returns sha256 hexdigest()[:12], twelve hex characters; the only other '' (line 83) is the not-a-file refusal, itself a failure. The docstring names '' as the failure value and the except logs the OSError. The caller can tell failure from an answer: '' is failure on both lines.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision; HELD in leg 7). File-wide because sleep_in_test passes no line (is_bypassed without a line, sleep_in_test_check.py 146); it covers exactly the three sleeps at 143, 168 and 228. 143 and 168 are the 1ms yields between turns of the racer's writer and readers. The yield is the subject: Windows share-mode refuses os.replace on an open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, and zero-delay loops starved CI to reads == 0 (08-18, 08-28). 228 is the timed race window, whose length is the exposure. The start already waits on the real condition (the _saw_read and _saw_write Events); no event marks enough interleavings, so there is nothing to poll.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision; HELD in leg 7): importlib.import_module in test_the_denier_actually_denies is the negative control. Its subject is the import attempt under the denier; a top-level import would succeed before the denier exists and prove nothing. The sys.modules delitems only drop cached aipass.memory modules so the finder is consulted, and monkeypatch restores them.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): None is never a registry here. The other None (line 115) is the not-found refusal, logged by logger.warning; it is a failure. The docstring names None as missing/unreadable, and every caller (update_ops 337, mint_ops 190, sync_registry_ops 401, mint_verify 94, regenerate_registry_ops 87) reads None as no registry.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): handle_command answers an exit code, 0 success and 1 failure (docstring). The other return 1 the checker counts as success (line 96) is the no-argument refusal, reported by warning('Usage: ...') and the usage lines; it is a failure. Every 1 here is a failure, and spawn.py's exit seam reads it so.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): the function answers an exit code, 0 success and 1 failure. The other return 1 (line 139) follows error(reason) on a refused ceremony with a console.print() between; it is a failure. Every 1 here is a failure, and spawn.py's exit seam reads it so.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): _handle_relocate answers an exit code, 0 success and 1 failure. The other return 1 (line 112) follows error('--relocate requires @branch and new_path') and the warning with its usage line; it is a failure. Every 1 here is a failure, and spawn.py's exit seam reads it so.

CHECKER DEFECT (fleet green leg 8, spawn's decision): _handle_check answers an exit code, 0 clean and 1 not clean. The other return 1 (line 171) is the not-clean verdict, reported by error('Owner/identity check: N issue(s)') and the issue lines; it is a failure. Every 1 here is a failure, and spawn.py's exit seam reads it so.
